entries.definition: A real parameter t in R used to order events; differences delta t = t2 - t1 are durations.
A convention for assigning spatial coordinates and a time coordinate to events: an origin, a set of basis vectors, and a clock.
An idealised object whose spatial extent and internal structure are neglected.
The location of a point-particle at time t in a reference-frame, represented by a vector r(t) in R^3.
The change in position: delta r = r(t2) - r(t1).
v(t) = dr/dt.
The scalar magnitude of velocity: speed(t) = ||v(t)||.
a(t) = dv/dt = d^2 r/dt^2.
The map t -> r(t) giving the position of a point-particle over some interval I subset R.
A set of points {r0 + lambda u : lambda in R} for fixed r0 in R^3 and nonzero direction u in R^3.
For a differentiable trajectory from t1 to t2, the arc length is s = integral of ||v(t)|| dt.
For two point-particle|s in the same reference-frame, the relative-position is r12(t) = r2(t) - r1(t).
For two point-particle|s in the same reference-frame, the relative-velocity is v12(t) = v2(t) - v1(t) = dr12/dt.

The state of being either stationary or moving along a straight-line with constant speed. Equivalently, a point-particle is in uniform-motion on an interval I if its velocity is constant throughout I; i.e. for all t1, t2 in I, v(t1) = v(t2). A point-particle is in uniform-motion at time t0 if there exists epsilon > 0 such that it is in uniform-motion on (t0 - epsilon, t0 + epsilon).
The state of motion exhibited by a free-particle when described in an inertial-frame.
A reference-frame in which every free-particle exhibits uniform-motion.
A point-particle that, when described in an inertial-frame, exhibits uniform-motion.
A reference-frame standard for Newtonian analysis of motion; historically, a Galilean reference frame.
A point-particle not subject to external influence relevant to its motion.
The acceleration of a point-particle as measured in an inertial-frame.
For a point-particle, inertial-acceleration equals net-force divided by inertial-mass: a = F/m.
The vector quantity satisfying net-force = inertial-mass times inertial-acceleration for a point-particle.
The positive scalar coefficient m such that net-force = m times inertial-acceleration for a point-particle.
net-force on particle p at time t is the vector sum of the impressed-force contribution supplied to p by every interaction in the closed interaction-set for p at t.
The closed set of all and only the independently warranted interaction|s relevant to particle p at time t; each member interaction supplies a target-directed impressed-force on p.

The target-directed vector force-action that an interaction in a particle's interaction-set supplies to that particle in a fixed context; it is the contribution summed to obtain the particle's net-force.
An abstract object-type.
An abstract object-type specified by class-specific-features; an object x is treated as an instance-of the raw-class when it is recognized as possessing the class-specific-features.
The set of features that specify a raw-class C; these features are whatever a modeler must recognize x as having in order to treat x as an instance-of C.
x is treated as an instance of a raw-class C when x is recognized as possessing the class-specific-features of C.
An impressed-force is a force-contribution that is either a canonical-force_acting-object or a reaction-force_acting-object.
A canonical-force_acting-object is an impressed-force designated as canonical; the corresponding reaction-force_acting-object is the impressed-force defined as the negative of it.
A reaction-force_acting-object is an impressed-force defined as the negative of canonical-force_acting-object.
An acting-object is an object equipped with both an activation-condition_acting-object and a corresponding canonical-force_acting-object.
If a point-particle fulfills the activation-condition_acting-object of an acting-object, the canonical-force_acting-object of that acting-object will be an impressed-force on the point-particle.
The canonical-force_acting-object is the impressed-force that an acting-object exerts on a point-particle that fulfills the activation-condition_acting-object.

The mechanical-composition_point-particle of a point-particle is the set of acting-object|s that the point-particle has. When a point-particle serves as the representative, or centre of mass, of a body, all acting-object|s of that body are included in the mechanical-composition_point-particle of that point-particle.

The paired-particle_acting-object of an acting-object is the point-particle whose mechanical-composition_point-particle includes that acting-object. The acting-object is modelled as located at the position of its paired-particle_acting-object.
An arbitrary subset of particles selected by the observer for analysis.
For a particle p in a mechanical-system S at time t, an interaction-candidate is any interaction in the interaction-set for p at t.
An interaction-candidate is an elementary force-unit, every one of which must be able to be placed in an interaction-pair for the mechanical-system to be a mechanically-closed-system.
An interaction-pair is the form into which each interaction-candidate is placed in a mechanically-closed-system.
A mechanically-closed-system is a mechanical-system in which every interaction-candidate can be placed in an interaction-pair.

Two interaction-candidate|s form an interaction-pair when they correspond to the same acting-object, one being the canonical-force_acting-object associated with that acting-object and the other being the reaction-force_acting-object associated with that acting-object, the latter exerted on the paired-particle_acting-object.
A mechanically-closed-system is a mechanical-system whose future behaviour is determined by the equations produced from the interactions internal to it.
